sections.h2: Where is the Davidson County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is in the Public Square Garage at 300 Deaderick Street, Nashville, TN 37201. Staff work the counter on weekdays between 8:00 in the morning and 4:30 in the afternoon. Call 615-862-6790. Letters go to Post Office Box 196398, Nashville, TN 37219-6398, but a courier other than the U.S. Postal Service must use the street address.

Davidson County keeps its warranty deeds, deeds of trust, releases, powers of attorney, liens and plats here. When you sell a house anywhere in the county, the deed your buyer signs ends up in these records, and so does the paper that clears your old mortgage.

City and county share one government, called Metro Nashville, so the register is a Metro department and its pages live on nashville.gov.

sections.h2: The register's app and online tools
sections.html:
A free mobile app, listed in the Apple and Google stores as Nashville - Davidson Co. ROD, puts several office services on a phone. It includes a fee calculator, buttons to call or email the staff, and the Property Alert sign-up.

Property Alert deserves a minute of a seller's time. Any filing under your name triggers an email, so an attempt to record a forged deed against your house would reach you quickly. The sign-up is free.

  • Fee calculator for recording charges, on the office website and in the app
  • Property Alert email notices for filings under your name
  • Online searching of recorded documents by subscription

Staff will not draw up a deed, because a deed is a legal document and an attorney should prepare it. They also will not run a title search to tell you about liens, though the indexes are on public computers for anyone to use.

sections.h2: Charges for a Davidson County deed copy
sections.html:
Plain copies run fifty cents a page. Certified ones run a dollar a page. Those rates hold at the counter and by post, though postal requests have a two-dollar floor.

Uncertified copy$0.50 per pageIn person or by mail
Certified copy$1 per pageIn person or by mail

In person the office takes cash, checks, credit cards and money orders. A faxed copy is $1 a page, but only for customers who have opened an escrow account with the office first.

When you write for a copy, give the property address. If you want something other than a property deed, send as many details as you can so staff can find it in the indexes.

sections.h2: What gets a Nashville deed turned away?
sections.html:
The register decides only whether a paper can be accepted for recording and leaves the question of legal soundness to the lawyer who drafted it. A deed has to carry the following:

  • Legible text with a notarized acknowledgment, since every signature is notarized
  • Names and addresses for the owner and the taxpayer, under Tennessee Code section 66-24-114
  • A derivation clause that cites the earlier recorded deed, section 66-24-110
  • Name and address of whoever drafted it, section 66-24-115
  • The parcel number, section 66-24-122
  • Fees and any transfer tax due on the day it is filed

Only originals are taken. A certified copy of something already recorded with another government office is the single exception. When a deed calls for an oath of consideration, that oath gets its own notary stamp. A missing parcel number or preparer's name is a common reason a recording is refused. Have the closing attorney compare this list with your deed before you sign.

sections.h2: What transfer tax does a Nashville sale trigger?
sections.html:
On a sale, the realty transfer tax comes to 37 cents per $100 of the price. The buyer, as grantee, hands it to the register along with the deed. A new loan adds a mortgage tax of 11.5 cents per $100 of debt past the first $2,000, paid by the borrower.

The tax follows the actual price or market value on your deed, so your own contract number is the one that counts. Middle-of-the-market owner-occupied value is $417,400.

An exempt transfer needs no oath of value. Transfers that end a tenancy by the entirety, divisions of land held in common, and leasehold estates are among the exempt kinds.

Davidson County had an estimated 745,904 residents in July 2025, against 715,887 at the 2020 base. With owners in only 52.8 percent of homes, nearly half of households rent. Typical rent is $1,582 a month, typical household income is $77,853, and there were 389,379 housing units and 5,632 building permits in 2025. A seller with a dated or inherited house faces a large pool of renters and newcomers, and a cash sale is one route to weigh against a listing.

sections.h2: Where does recording leave a seller on the tax bill?
sections.html:
Recording changes the name on the public record and has no effect on what is owed. The January 1 assessment drives the tax. Payment opens the first Monday of October, and a balance left after February is delinquent.

Before you close, ask the Metropolitan Trustee what stands against your parcel. The Trustee keeps weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. A value dispute begins at the county equalization board. If it is still unresolved, the State Board of Equalization is the next stop. Its cutoff is August 1, or 45 days after the local notice if that comes later.

Owners who are 65 or disabled may receive state tax relief on up to $33,600 of value if income stayed at or under $38,470. Applications go through the trustee.

sections.h2: What to do before you sign a Nashville deed
sections.html:
A short routine keeps a recording from bouncing and a closing from slipping.

  1. Have the attorney or title company draft the deed, because register staff will not.
  2. Check that the parcel number, the drafter's name and address, and the owner and taxpayer addresses are all on it.
  3. Sign before a notary, and add a separate notary stamp if the deed calls for an oath of consideration.
  4. Use the fee calculator to estimate recording charges, and plan for the transfer tax at 37 cents per $100.
  5. Ask the Metropolitan Trustee for the balance on the parcel, so any open tax is paid from the proceeds at closing.
  6. Sign up for Property Alert so you hear about any later filing under your name.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in Davidson County?
faqs.a: The register of deeds does, at the Public Square Garage, 300 Deaderick Street, Nashville. The phone is 615-862-6790, and the records include deeds, deeds of trust, releases, liens and plats.

faqs.q: Will the register take a photocopy of my deed?
faqs.a: Only a certified copy of something already recorded with another government office. Everything else has to be an original, signed and notarized.

faqs.q: What does a recorded deed copy cost in Davidson County?
faqs.a: Fifty cents a page plain and a dollar a page certified. Mailed requests cost at least $2, and a mailed subdivision plat is $5.

faqs.q: Can the Davidson County register tell me about liens on my house?
faqs.a: No. Finding liens takes a title search by an attorney or title company. You may use the public indexes on the office computers yourself, but staff do not write deeds either.

faqs.q: How do I get a warning if someone files a deed in my name?
faqs.a: Join Property Alert, the register's free service, on the office website or in the app. Any document filed under your name then sends you an email.
